examples.text: I hold BTC. By Dec 31 my loss starts at zero at 70,000 and grows steadily to $10,000 at 60,000, then stays at $10,000 below that. I can spend $500 to cover this loss.
I own BTC and want protection if it ends below 60,000 by Dec 31. My budget is $300, but I have not decided how much loss to cover.
I own BTC. If it ends below 60,000 by Dec 31, my loss could be $5,000 or $15,000. I am not sure which amount to insure. I can spend $300.

I hold BTC. I lose $8,000 if BTC ever touches 60,000 before Dec 31, even if it recovers and finishes above 60,000. I need that touch-triggered payment, not protection based on the final price. My budget is $300.
I run outdoor events in Chicago and lose $12000 if the daily high is below 60°F on September 26. My protection budget is $600.
I operate a nursery in Berlin and lose $5000 if the daily minimum temperature falls below -5°C on December 31. My hedge budget is $300.
I operate outdoor events in Phoenix and lose $10000 if the daily maximum temperature exceeds 110°F on September 26. My hedge budget is $500.
I have floating rate debt and lose $20000 if the Fed rate is above 5% by December 31. My hedge budget is $500.
I hold gold and lose $5000 if its price ends below $3500 per ounce by December 31. My hedge budget is $300.
